# d3-hierarchy treemap differential fixtures

Each JSON file is one tree and the exact rectangles `d3-hierarchy` 3.1.2 produced for
it, with the `d3-hierarchy` copy Mermaid 12.3.0 depends on, under
`research/mermaid-port/upstream/mermaid/node_modules/.pnpm/d3-hierarchy@3.1.2/node_modules/d3-hierarchy/src`.

They are generated by `generate.mjs`:

```sh
node generate.mjs
```

The script builds `hierarchy(tree).sum((d) => d.value ?? 0).sort((a, b) => (b.value ?? 0) - (a.value ?? 0))`
and runs `treemap()` with the fixture's size, tile, padding, and rounding, then records
`root.descendants()` in order. Node identity is the path `generate.mjs` assigns: the
child indices from the root, joined with `.` (`""` for the root itself).

A padding is a number, or `{ "if_children": [a, b] }` for Mermaid's
`d.children && d.children.length > 0 ? a : b`. `tile` is one of `squarify`,
`squarify-ratio`, `binary`, `dice`, `slice`, `sliceDice`, `resquarify`, or
`resquarify-ratio`; a ratio is carried in `ratio`.

The fixtures cover a flat tree, a wide flat tree, two and three levels, zero values
(including a zero total), every tiling method on the same tree, Mermaid's section padding
functions with rounding, constant inner and outer padding, and the same padding on a flat
tree. JSON has no NaN, so `JSON.stringify` writes one as `null`.

`differential.rs` rebuilds each tree through this port's `Hierarchy`, `sum`, `sort_by`,
and `Treemap`, and compares every node's depth, value, and `x0`/`y0`/`x1`/`y1` within
`1e-6`.
